cls: Inactivated (killed) viral vaccine - active immunisation against hepatitis A
pharm: A sterile suspension of formaldehyde-inactivated, alum-adsorbed hepatitis A virus that stimulates protective anti-HAV antibodies
quick: 1.0 mL IM (e.g. Havrix 1440 EL.U.), then a booster 6-12 months later
Inactivated vaccine; may be given if indicated (e.g. risk of exposure) - weigh benefit
No dose adjustment; useful in those with chronic liver disease at risk
No interaction with the vaccine itself
Observe for hypersensitivity after injection; ensure 2-dose completion
summary: Inactivated hepatitis A vaccine provides active immunisation against disease caused by hepatitis A virus (HAV) and is approved for persons 12 months of age and older. It is a sterile injectable suspension of formaldehyde-inactivated, aluminium-adsorbed virus given intramuscularly. Using Havrix as a representative product: each 1.0 mL adult dose contains 1440 ELISA units (EL.U.) of viral antigen and each 0.5 mL paediatric dose contains 720 EL.U. The schedule is a single dose followed by a booster 6-12 months later (adults 1.0 mL then 1.0 mL; children/adolescents 0.5 mL then 0.5 mL). Primary immunisation should be completed at least 2 weeks before expected exposure. It is highly effective and is recommended for travellers to endemic areas, people at occupational or behavioural risk, those with chronic liver disease, and routine childhood immunisation in many programmes.
indications: Active immunisation against hepatitis A virus infection in persons 12 months of age and older
Pre-exposure protection for travellers to endemic regions and other at-risk groups

dosage.d: 0.5 mL (720 EL.U.) primary dose, then a 0.5 mL booster
dosage.t: Booster 6 to 12 months after the first dose
dosage.n: Intramuscular; doses for the Havrix product

dosage.d: 1.0 mL (1440 EL.U.) primary dose, then a 1.0 mL booster
dosage.t: Booster 6 to 12 months after the first dose

dosage.d: Complete primary dose at least 2 weeks before expected exposure
dosage.n: Product-specific antigen content/schedule may vary between brands

admin: Administer intramuscularly into the deltoid (adults and older children) or anterolateral thigh (younger children); do not give intravenously, intradermally or subcutaneously routinely
Shake well before use to obtain a uniform, turbid white suspension; do not use if it looks otherwise or contains particulates
Use a separate sterile syringe/needle and separate site for any concurrent vaccines
Have epinephrine and resuscitation equipment available for rare anaphylaxis
Ensure the 6-12 month booster is given to achieve long-term protection
Record the dose; defer in moderate or severe acute illness
moa: The vaccine contains hepatitis A virus that has been propagated in cell culture, purified, and inactivated with formaldehyde, then adsorbed onto an aluminium adjuvant. When injected, the inactivated viral antigens are processed by the immune system and induce production of neutralising anti-HAV IgG antibodies and immune memory. These antibodies provide active, durable protection against subsequent infection with wild-type hepatitis A virus. Because the virus is inactivated (killed), the vaccine cannot cause hepatitis A infection.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylaxis) to a previous dose or to any vaccine component (including neomycin where present)
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness (defer until recovered)
Bleeding disorders/anticoagulation (use care with IM injection)
Immunocompromise may blunt the antibody response

preg: As an inactivated vaccine, the theoretical risk to the fetus is low. It may be given during pregnancy when the woman is at risk of hepatitis A exposure (e.g. travel to endemic areas), weighing the benefit of protection against the limited data.
lact: Inactivated hepatitis A vaccine is considered compatible with breastfeeding and may be given to nursing mothers when indicated.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment; the response may be reduced in advanced renal disease/dialysis, and completion of the schedule is important.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required. Vaccination is specifically recommended for susceptible people with chronic liver disease, who are at higher risk of severe hepatitis A.

major: No clinically significant drug interactions; efficacy may be reduced by immunosuppressive therapy
moderate: Immunosuppressants/high-dose corticosteroids - may diminish the antibody response
Concurrent immune globulin - may slightly lower antibody titres but is generally acceptable when both are indicated
minor: Other inactivated vaccines can usually be co-administered at separate sites
interactions.alcohol: No interaction with the vaccine itself
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically important interference; induces anti-HAV antibodies (expected after vaccination)

rare: Syncope around the time of injection
emergency: Anaphylaxis (urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension) - treat with epinephrine and supportive care

monitoring: Observe for about 15 minutes after injection for immediate hypersensitivity/syncope
Documentation and completion of the 2-dose series
Serology generally not needed routinely in immunocompetent people
counsel: This vaccine protects against hepatitis A, a liver infection; you need two doses - the second 6 to 12 months after the first
Get the first dose at least 2 weeks before travelling to a higher-risk area
A sore arm, mild headache or tiredness for a day or two is common and settles
The vaccine is made from killed virus and cannot give you hepatitis A
Tell the clinician about severe allergies; seek urgent help for any breathing difficulty, swelling or rash after the injection
pk: Protective anti-HAV antibodies in most recipients by about 2-4 weeks after the first dose
Robust antibody response after the primary dose; boosted further by the second dose
Not applicable (vaccine elicits an endogenous antibody response)
Long-term protection - estimated to persist for many years (likely decades) after the two-dose series
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C; do NOT freeze; protect from light; discard if frozen
pearls: Two-dose IM series: primary dose then a booster 6-12 months later gives long-lasting (likely lifelong) protection
Adult Havrix dose 1.0 mL = 1440 EL.U.; paediatric (12 months-18 years) 0.5 mL = 720 EL.U. - product-specific
Inactivated (killed) vaccine - cannot cause hepatitis A and is safe to give in immunocompromise (though response may be lower)
Recommended for travellers, at-risk groups and people with chronic liver disease; complete >=2 weeks before exposure
Do NOT freeze - freezing destroys the alum-adsorbed antigen
missed: If the booster (second) dose is delayed, it can still be given later without restarting the series - simply complete the two doses. Keep the appointment for the second dose 6-12 months after the first to ensure durable protection.
overdose: Overdose is not a meaningful concern for a single standardised vaccine dose. Inadvertent administration of an extra or larger dose is managed by observation; no specific treatment is required beyond routine monitoring for local/systemic reactions.
